title: A governed retail reporting store
context: Aurora needs to load structured sales transactions in batches. Finance analysts use T-SQL heavily and need governed enterprise BI reporting. Device telemetry is handled by another team.
question: Where should Priya begin for this reporting workload?

options.label: Warehouse
options.explanation: Warehouse best matches structured relational data, T-SQL, and enterprise BI requirements.

options.label: Lakehouse
options.explanation: Lakehouse can support analytics and engineering, but the stated relational T-SQL reporting requirements make Warehouse the stronger fit.

options.label: Eventhouse
options.explanation: Eventhouse is intended for event and telemetry analysis, which the scenario explicitly puts elsewhere.

decisiveClue: Structured transactions + T-SQL + governed BI are the requirements that matter; the telemetry detail is not part of this workload.

title: One report, different regional views
context: Jonas can open Aurora’s Sales report. He must see only Norway rows while Sweden managers use the same report and semantic model to see Sweden rows.
question: Which control should Leila configure?

options.label: Row-level security on the semantic model
options.explanation: RLS filters model rows for the signed-in identity while allowing users to open the same report.

options.label: A separate item permission for each region
options.explanation: Item permission determines access to an item, not which subset of rows appears after it opens.

options.label: Object-level security for the sales table
options.explanation: OLS hides a table or object entirely; Jonas still needs the sales table, filtered to Norway.

decisiveClue: The requirement is about a different subset of rows after the report opens, which points specifically to RLS.

title: Fresh analysis over large Delta tables
context: Aurora stores large sales tables as Delta tables in OneLake. Marta wants interactive analytics without relying on a traditional full Import refresh before report queries run.
question: Which storage mode most directly fits the scenario?

options.label: Direct Lake
options.explanation: Direct Lake is designed to query required Delta-table columns from OneLake for interactive analytics without the traditional full Import-copy path.

options.label: Import
options.explanation: Import depends on a copied in-memory model refreshed on a schedule, which conflicts with the stated requirement.

options.label: DirectQuery
options.explanation: DirectQuery is a source-query path; the OneLake Delta-table and no-traditional-Import clues point to Direct Lake.

decisiveClue: The combination of Delta tables in OneLake, interactive analytics, and avoiding a traditional full Import refresh is decisive.

title: Shared customer accounts
context: Some Aurora customers hold several purchasing accounts. Some accounts are shared by several customer entities. Finance needs balances by customer without duplicating balance facts.
question: Which model design fits this requirement?

options.label: Use a CustomerAccount bridge table between Customer and Account
options.explanation: A bridge records the shared associations while preserving each balance fact once.

options.label: Create a direct many-to-many relationship from Customer to FactBalance
options.explanation: This skips the account association and makes filtering harder to reason about.

options.label: Duplicate balance rows once for each linked customer
options.explanation: Duplicating facts would overstate balances when totals are calculated.

decisiveClue: Both sides can have several associations, but the facts must not be duplicated: that is the bridge-table pattern.

title: A retried API call duplicates order lines
context: Aurora’s daily order export occasionally lands the same order line twice because a retried API call resubmitted it. Separately, OrderDate arrives as inconsistent text such as “2026-03-08” and “03/08/2026”.
question: Which operation fixes the retried-call problem specifically, without touching OrderDate values?

options.label: Remove duplicate rows using the order line key
options.explanation: Yes. This removes the repeated record introduced by the retry while leaving other columns untouched.

options.label: Change OrderDate to a date type
options.explanation: This resolves the inconsistent date text, not the duplicated order line.

options.label: Merge queries on OrderID
options.explanation: Merging combines data from another query; it does not remove a row duplicated by a retried call.

decisiveClue: A row repeated because of a retried call is a duplicate-row problem, distinct from the separate date-format issue in the same scenario.

title: A repeating loyalty rate is not a fact
context: Aurora’s raw sales export includes a loyalty-tier discount rate on every order line. The same rate repeats across every row for a given customer, and Marta wants to group revenue by loyalty tier.
question: Where should the loyalty discount rate live in the star schema?

options.label: Move it into DimCustomer as a loyalty-tier attribute
options.explanation: Yes. A value that describes a customer and repeats across many rows belongs in the customer dimension.

options.label: Keep it in FactSales next to Revenue
options.explanation: Keeping a repeating descriptive attribute in the fact table duplicates it onto every event row and makes grouping harder to reuse.

options.label: Turn it into a DAX measure
options.explanation: The rate is a stored descriptive attribute of the customer, not a calculation over filter context.

decisiveClue: A value that describes an entity and repeats across many transaction rows belongs in a dimension, not duplicated onto every fact row.

title: Same question, three engines
context: An analyst wants total revenue by region for the last 30 days. The rows live in a Warehouse table. A separate Eventhouse holds device ping counts for the same period, and a semantic model has not been built over either yet.
question: Which language is the closest fit for filtering and aggregating the Warehouse table directly?

options.label: T-SQL
options.explanation: Yes. Warehouse exposes a relational T-SQL endpoint suited to filtering and aggregating its tables directly.

options.label: KQL
options.explanation: KQL is the query language for Eventhouse and Real-Time Intelligence, not the Warehouse’s relational tables.

options.label: DAX
options.explanation: DAX operates over a semantic model’s relationships and filter context; no semantic model exists yet in this scenario.

decisiveClue: The question asks about querying the Warehouse table directly, before any semantic model or event store is involved.

title: A Direct Lake report starts routing through the SQL endpoint
context: Aurora’s Direct Lake model over FactSales normally serves report queries straight from OneLake columns. A security engineer then defines row-level security directly on the SQL analytics endpoint for FactSales. The same report queries now come back through the SQL analytics endpoint instead.
question: What is the most direct explanation for the shift?

options.label: The model falls back to the SQL analytics endpoint because row-level security is defined there
options.explanation: Yes. Row-level security defined at the SQL analytics endpoint is a documented Direct Lake fallback trigger to DirectQuery through that endpoint.

options.label: Direct Lake is broken and needs to be rebuilt
options.explanation: This is documented fallback behavior, not a failure — nothing about the model needs rebuilding.

options.label: The model silently switched to a full Import refresh
options.explanation: Direct Lake does not convert itself into an Import model; the documented behavior is a query-path fallback, not a refresh-mode change.

decisiveClue: Row-level security applied at the SQL analytics endpoint is the specific, documented condition that routes Direct Lake queries through DirectQuery instead.

title: Late-arriving orders in a rolling window
context: Aurora’s FactSales incremental refresh policy keeps 5 years of history and refreshes only the last 10 days. A distribution partner occasionally reports order corrections up to 20 days after the original sale.
question: What should Priya change so those late corrections are captured without reprocessing all 5 years?

options.label: Increase the refresh (incremental) range to cover at least 20 days
options.explanation: Yes. The refresh range must cover the realistic lateness window, independent of how much history is retained.

options.label: Switch to a full refresh of the whole table on every run
options.explanation: This reprocesses far more than necessary and undermines the purpose of incremental refresh.

options.label: Shorten the historical retention window to 20 days
options.explanation: Retention controls how much history stays in the table; it does not change whether recent late-arriving rows get refreshed.

decisiveClue: The refresh range must cover the realistic lateness window, which is a separate policy from historical retention.

title: Ten measures, repeated time intelligence
context: Aurora’s model already defines ten base measures, including Total Sales and Total Cost. Marta now wants a Year-to-Date and Prior-Year version of every one of them, and the modeler wants to avoid writing twenty nearly identical DAX measures.
question: What is the most direct way to add YTD and Prior-Year variants for every base measure?

options.label: Build a calculation group with YTD and Prior-Year calculation items
options.explanation: Yes. A calculation group applies the same time-intelligence pattern across every existing and future base measure without duplicating DAX.

options.label: Duplicate each measure and wrap it in the matching time-intelligence function
options.explanation: This works but multiplies maintenance for every future base measure, which a calculation group is designed to avoid.

options.label: Add a new relationship to a second date-table copy
options.explanation: An extra date-table relationship does not by itself produce YTD or Prior-Year variants.

decisiveClue: Reusing one time-intelligence pattern across many existing measures without duplicating DAX per measure is the calculation-group scenario.
